1,621,650 km2 for 1864-1869: unchanged frontier.

1,624,460 km2 for 1873-1879 against the infobox 'about 1,300,000 km2' for 1873: ratio 0.80, within a factor of two; the shape follows the area of modern Iran.

1,624,363 km2 for 1880-1894. The Treaty of Akhal (21 September 1881) ended Iran's claims to Turkestan and Transoxiana, with the Atrek River as the boundary, and Merv, Sarakhs and Ashgabat were transferred to Russian control in 1884 (Qajar Iran page). Cliopatria's Qajar shape never included that steppe, so no cell changes.

1,624,363 km2 for 1898-1914, the same frontier. In 1907 'the British and Russian Empires partitioned Iran into spheres of influence' (Russian north, British south-east, a neutral zone): influence, not territory, so the shape stands. Russian troops held Tabriz from 1909 and Urmia and Khoi from 1910 (ledger, occupation).

correction.text: the full 1914 frontier of Iran: Persia declared neutrality and kept its sovereignty over the land the Russian, Ottoman and British armies occupied

Persia 'declared its neutrality' and stayed sovereign; the foreign armies were occupiers, so the whole 1914 shape stays Qajar and the cut-outs are drawn as occupations (ledger).

The frontier does not change.

region.text: Mazandaran, conquered by Agha Mohammad Khan from his brothers on 2 April 1779

ledger.note: 2 April 1779: the first land of the Qajar polity. After Karim Khan's death ('On 1 March 1779, while Agha Mohammad Khan was hunting, he was informed by Khadija Begum that Karim Khan had died') he defeated his brothers Reza Qoli and Morteza Qoli 'on 2 April, conquering Mazandaran' (Agha Mohammad Khan page; the sentence has no year, the 1779 comes from the sentence before it). Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026) moves the founding of this dossier from 1789 to this date so the north of Iran that the zand-dynasty ledger hands to 'qajar-dynasty' from 1779 to 1788 is not nobody's land (up to 1,663 cells in 1782-1788, window p1780-p1789); 1789 is the year he was 'enthroned as the king of Iran ... (but not yet crowned)' and the page's 'start of his reign', not the start of the polity ('It appears that during this period [1785-1786], Agha Mohammad Khan saw himself as the king of Iran, although he avoided using the title shah').

region.text: Hamadan: 'At the same time, his men captured Hamadan' (summer 1785)

ledger.note: Mirror of the zand-dynasty ledger loss of the same date (fix fx-45, 2 Nov 2026). Agha Mohammad Khan page: 'At the same time, his men captured Hamadan' (summer 1785 in the Zand ledger and the page's 'During the summer of 1785').

region.text: Azerbaijan: the Talysh, Sarab and Ardabil khanates and Qaradagh

ledger.note: 1791: Agha Mohammad Khan conquers Azerbaijan. In the spring of 1791 he marched into Azerbaijan and subdued the Talysh, Sarab and Ardabil khanates, going on to Qaradagh.

region.text: the Zand south: Fars with Shiraz, and Kerman

ledger.note: 1792: the Qajar advance on Fars. Agha Mohammad Khan 'set foot in Shiraz on 21 July 1792'; Lotf Ali Khan Zand had beaten Hajji Ebrahim's Qajar-backed forces in late 1791 or early 1792 and kept the south until 1794.
1794: Kerman falls and the Zand are finished. 'The city fell on 24 October' and 'in 1794 he defeated his last major competitor', with immense destruction of Kerman.

region.text: the last Zand territory: Shiraz and Kerman

ledger.note: 1794: the Qajar take Fars and Kerman, ending the Zand dynasty. The page names Shiraz (1792) and Kerman (1794); Fars and Sistan as provinces are my reading, and the Cliopatria shape adds both in 1794.

1795: the Qajar besiege Shusha. He besieged Shusha between 8 July and 9 August 1795 but accepted a settlement without entering the city; the same page elsewhere says he was killed in Shusha in 1797 'three days after he had taken the city', so the page disagrees with itself.

region.text: the kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti with Tbilisi

ledger.note: 1795: Agha Mohammad Khan invades Georgia. 'In August 1795, Agha Mohammad Khan crossed the Aras River' with the support of the khans of Erivan and Ganja; Tbilisi falls early on 11 September ('In a few hours, Agha Mohammad Khan was in full control of the Georgian capital', Agha Mohammad Khan page) and the infobox gives 'Annexation of Georgia: 11 September 1795'.
1795: the Shusha siege ends in a settlement on 9 August. The Karabakh Khanate is not entered.

region.text: the khanates of Karabakh, Ganja and Erivan

ledger.note: 1796: Cliopatria draws the Erivan, Karabakh and Ganja khanates as Qajar land. The pages show the khans of Erivan and Ganja backing the 1795 campaign and Shusha settling, but do not say they became provinces or vassals; bridging at confidence 1 (status and year unsettled).

1796: Agha Mohammad Khan takes Khorasan. He 'entered Mashhad on 14 May' a year after the Caucasus campaign (the page gives no explicit year); Cliopatria shows half of Khorasan Durrani until 1796 and the Qajar in full from 1797. The page does not name Mashhad's ruler; the counterpart is the Afsharid rump state of Shahrokh at Mashhad, whose own dossier (afsharid-iran) ends in 1796 with the Qajar seizure of Mashhad.

1797: Cliopatria's shape adds Shirvan, Sheki and Baku. None of the pages opened dates their submission to the Qajar (the Russian-war page shows them under Persian suzerainty when Russia took them in 1805-06); bridging at confidence 1.

1801: Russia annexes Kartli-Kakheti. Russia annexed Kartli-Kakheti on 12 September 1801 after its troops marched into Tbilisi in 1799 (Qajar Iran page); the Russian-war page (1804-1813) has the annexation in December 1800.

region.text: the khanates south of the Caucasus: Ganja, Karabakh, Shaki, Shirvan, Baku, Derbent, Quba, Erivan and Nakhchivan

ledger.note: 1804: Russia takes Ganja and the Russo-Persian war begins. Ganja was captured on 15 January 1804 and the infobox dates the war 22 June 1804 - 24 October 1813.
1804: Ganja falls to Russia on 15 January; its governor Javad Khan is killed.
1805: Karabakh and Shaki submit to Russia. Karabakh on 14 May (the year is 1805 by context), Shaki on 21 May 1805.
1805: Russia accepts the submission of Shirvan on 27 December (the year is 1805 by context).
1806: Baku is surrendered to Russia. General Tsitsianov was murdered on 8 February 1806 while accepting Baku's surrender.

region.text: Georgia, Southern Dagestan, most of Azerbaijan and minor parts of Armenia

ledger.note: 1813: the Treaty of Gulistan. the infobox: 'Persia is forced to cede what is now Georgia, Southern Dagestan, most of Azerbaijan' and minor parts of northern Armenia; Persia kept Meghri and the northern Talysh border was left for later decision. The infobox end date is 24 October 1813 (an armistice was made in October); the Cliopatria shape had already shed these lands in 1805-06. Region: Azerbaijan without Nakhchivan, which stayed Persian until Turkmenchay (1828, ledger) (reviewer fix).

region.text: the khanates south of the Caucasus

ledger.note: 1813: the first Russo-Persian war ends in a Russian victory with the Treaty of Gulistan (infobox end 24 October 1813).

region.text: Erivan and Nakhchivan, with fighting in Talysh, Karabakh and Ganja

ledger.note: 1826: the second Russo-Persian war begins. The infobox gives 8 July 1826 - 2 February 1828; Russia took Bash Aparan on 8 July, fighting in Talysh began 25-26 July and Iranian forces took Lankaran and Saliyan on 12 August 1826.
1827: Tabriz surrenders to Russia. It surrendered without a fight on 24 October 1827; Ardabil was captured and plundered on 25 January 1828.
1828: the Russians leave Tabriz and Ardabil. The page is silent on the withdrawal; bridging at the treaty year.

union.text: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand and Zahedan in what is now Iran

region.text: Persian Baluchistan: Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Zahedan and the Iranian Makran coast, held by the Khanate of Kalat

ledger.note: Early 19th century: the Khanate of Kalat 'declined in the early 19th century, losing much of its territory to Qajar Iran and Emirate of Afghanistan' (Khanate of Kalat page, no years). The Iranian share is drawn as the Persian Baluchistan conquests of Nasir Khan I (Khash, Bampur, Qasr-e Qand, Zahedan) and the Iranian Makran coast, at 1828 as a bridging choice; this mirrors khanate-of-kalat ledger[9]. The Sistan and Baluchestan province page puts the Khanate's rule of the province as late as 1896 (the Iran-Kalat border was demarcated in 1896 on the Khanate page): the pages disagree and neither dates the Qajar takeover.

region.text: Erivan and Nakhichevan provinces north of the Aras

ledger.note: 1828: the Treaty of Turkmenchay. 'Iran cedes its Erivan and Nakhichevan provinces to Russia'; the treaty 'stripped Iran of its last remaining territories north of Aras river', all of modern Armenia, the Nakhchivan AR and Iğdır Province. Abbas Mirza signed on 2 February 1828 on this page (the Qajar Iran page says 10 February).
1828: the war ends with the Treaty of Turkmenchay (2 February 1828).

1856: Persia takes Herat. Iran succeeded in taking Herat on 25 October 1856, after a nine-month siege (Qajar Iran page). Counterpart: the Principality of Herat; the Anglo-Persian War page says Herat had 'declared itself independent' under 'its own rebellious emir', and Dost Mohammad took it only in 1863 (reviewer fix).

region.text: Kharg Island, Bushehr, and in 1857 Mohammerah and Ahvaz

ledger.note: 1856: Britain lands in Persia. The British 'captured the island of Kharag on 4 December' and the city of Bushehr on 10 December 1856; Mohammerah fell on 27 March and Ahvaz on 1 April 1857.

1857: the Treaty of Paris, signed 4 March: the Shah 'agreed to withdraw from Herat'. Herat returned to Afghan control (Dost Mohammed retook it in 1863). Counterpart: the Principality of Herat (reviewer fix).
1857: the British leave Bushehr. 'In October, the British withdrew from Bushehr' (the page gives the month, the year follows the Treaty of Paris); it is silent on when Mohammerah and Ahvaz were left.
1909: Russia occupies Tabriz. 'Tabriz was occupied in 1909' (Persian campaign page).
1910: Russia occupies Urmia and Khoi. 'Urmia and Khoi in 1910' (Persian campaign page).
1915: Ottoman troops take Urmia. Omer Naci's volunteer detachment captured Urmia on 4 January 1915; the 'Mosul Group' entered Tabriz about a week later.
1915: an Ottoman column enters Tabriz about a week after Urmia fell (4 January 1915).
1915: Russia retakes Tabriz. Chernozubov entered Tabriz on 30 January 1915.

1915: the Ottoman presence around Urmia ends. The page gives no date; the Ottoman 1st Expeditionary Force was repulsed at Diliman on 15 April 1915 and the Russians held the north until 1917; bridging at confidence 1.

region.text: Bushire (Bushehr) and the south held by British forces

ledger.note: 1915: British forces occupy Bushehr in August 1915 and later raise the South Persia Rifles (1916); the British advance reached Kerman on 12 June 1916. Region: the south Cliopatria cuts out for the British colonial empire, my reading of an occupation whose extent the page does not give.

region.text: northern Persia from Tabriz to Hamadan held by Russian forces

ledger.note: 1915: the Russian army spreads across northern Persia. Russian forces took Tehran by the end of November 1915 (the page's wording) and Hamadan on 15 December 1915; they numbered 80,000-90,000 later in the war. Region: Cliopatria's Russian cut-out inside Persia.
1916: the Ottoman XIII Corps invades Persia. It crossed back on 8 June, captured Kermanshah on 2 July and Hamadan on 10 August 1916.
1916: the Russians retake the Hamadan front. in December 1916 Russian forces retook Qom and Hamadan; the page does not say when the Ottomans left Kermanshah.

1917: the Russian occupation of Tabriz collapses. The Revolution halted all Russian military operations; by November 1917 Baratov had barely one effective regiment, and Cliopatria's Russian cut-out is gone in 1917.
1917: the Russian occupation of Urmia and Khoi ends with the collapse of the Russian army ('no effective military force' for the rest of 1917).

region.text: northern Persia from Tabriz to Hamadan

ledger.note: 1917: the Russian zone across northern Persia dissolves; about 1,000 loyal Cossacks under Baratov still helped the British in February 1918.

region.text: the south and the Gilan coast held by British forces in 1918-19

ledger.note: 1918: British forces reach northern Persia. Dunsterforce was ordered to march through Persia to Anzali (Enzeli); in 1919 General Ironside occupied northern Persia to enforce the Armistice of Mudros. Cliopatria's British cut-out grows from 405 to 592 cells in 1918.

region.text: northern Persia from Tabriz to the southern Caspian shore

ledger.note: 1918: the Ottoman IV Corps re-enters Persia. It entered Tabriz on 8 June 1918, Urmia fell on 31 July and by September 1918 Ottoman forces controlled northern Persia from Tabriz to the southern Caspian shore.
1918: the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) ends the Ottoman occupation of northern Persia; the infobox lists the Ottoman withdrawal.
1920: Soviet ships enter Anzali. In May 1920 the 'Soviet Caspian Fleet, led by Fyodor Raskolnikov' entered the port and the British garrison 'evacuated the town without any resistance'.

1920: Mirza Kuchik Khan's Jangali partisans set up the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic in Gilan with Red Army help, capital Rasht. The infobox says 'Socialist Republic declared: May 1920' and the body 'In May 1920 ... came into being'; the intro says it 'lasted from June 1920'.

region.text: the south held by British forces

ledger.note: 1921: the British occupation of the south ends. The page is silent on the date British forces left; Cliopatria's British cut-out lasts to 1921 and is gone in 1922 (bridging at confidence 1).

region.text: northern Persia held by British forces

ledger.note: 1921: the British occupation of the north ends. The page is silent on the date British forces left; bridging at confidence 1 on Cliopatria's last British cut-out year.
1921: Soviet forces withdraw after the Russo-Persian treaty of February 1921, which 'ensured peaceful relations' and resulted in 'the withdrawal of Soviet forces'.
1921: the Gilan republic is crushed. It 'officially came to an end in September 1921' after Reza Khan's coup (February 1921); the Qajar government regains Gilan.

region.text: the whole of Iran, passed to Reza Shah Pahlavi

ledger.note: 1925: the Majles deposes Ahmad Shah and the Qajar dynasty ends. Infobox 'Deposed by Constituent Assembly: 31 October 1925'; Reza Khan is proclaimed Reza Shah Pahlavi (Qajar dynasty page: constituent assembly of 12 December 1925).

wars.name: Qajar-Zand wars
wars.outcome: Qajar victory: Lotf Ali Khan Zand is defeated at Kerman in 1794 (the city fell on 24 October) and the Zand dynasty ends.
wars.note: The page dates Jafar Khan Zand's murder to 23 January 1789, Lotf Ali's victory in the following civil war to May 1789 and the siege of Shiraz to 25 June - 7 September 1789.

wars.name: Persian invasion of Georgia (1795)
wars.outcome: Agha Mohammad Khan took and sacked Tbilisi on 11 September 1795; Russia annexed Kartli-Kakheti in 1801.
wars.note: He set out in May 1795 and crossed the Aras in August.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1804-1813)

zones.text: Ganja, Karabakh, Shaki, Shirvan, Baku, Derbent, Quba, Talysh, Erivan and Nakhchivan

wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Gulistan (24 October 1813) cedes Georgia, Southern Dagestan and most of Azerbaijan; Persia keeps Meghri, Erivan and Nakhchivan.
wars.note: The infobox dates the war 22 June 1804 - 24 October 1813; Ganja fell on 15 January 1804. The Ganja and Erivan khanates fought beside Persia.

wars.name: Russo-Persian War (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Turkmenchay (2 February 1828) takes the last Persian lands north of the Aras and a large indemnity.
wars.note: Etchmiadzin surrendered in April 1827, Abbasabad and Ordubad in July 1827, the Erivan citadel in September 1827, Tabriz on 24 October 1827 and Ardabil was taken on 25 January 1828.

wars.name: Anglo-Persian War
wars.outcome: British victory: Persia withdraws from Herat under the Treaty of Paris (4 March 1857) and the British leave the Gulf ports.
wars.note: Infobox 1 November 1856 - 4 April 1857. Iran took Herat on 25 October 1856; Britain took Kharg on 4 December and Bushehr on 10 December 1856.

wars.name: Persian campaign (World War I)

zones.text: north-western Persia, fought over by Russia and the Ottomans

wars.outcome: Allied victory with British control; Persia stayed neutral and kept its frontier. The Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) ended the Ottoman occupation.
wars.note: Dec 1914 - 30 Oct 1918. Persia is a victim, not a belligerent: the zones are occupations in the ledger.

wars.name: Soviet intervention in Gilan
wars.outcome: The Soviet fleet lands at Anzali in May 1920 and the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic holds Gilan until September 1921, when Reza Khan's government ends it.
wars.note: The page is silent on the 26 February 1921 date; the infobox says February 1921.

certainty.note: Fix fx-45: the polity of Agha Mohammad Khan before his enthronement of 1789 is drawn by events only (no Cliopatria shape before 1788); Isfahan, Hamadan and the Kurdish and Bakhtiari lands changed hands several times and the pages date few of the moves.
The frontiers with the Caucasus khanates, Georgia and the Durrani lands in Khorasan are tribal and vassal lines, not surveyed; the Aras becomes a treaty line only in 1828.

The Russian frontier is a treaty line: the Aras from Turkmenchay (1828) and the Atrek from the Treaty of Akhal (1881). The Ottoman and Afghan-Baluch frontiers were not opened within the page budget and stay soft.
Foreign armies occupy Persian land in 1909-21 and the central government controls little of the periphery; the pre-war frontier itself is unchanged.

notes:
Cliopatria rows and shapes: the 1895-1897 shape is a data error (it mixes Iran with an Indonesian polygon; use the 1894 shape). The 1915-1921 shapes cut the foreign-occupied land (767 cells in 1915, 785 in 1916, 407 in 1917, 595 in 1918, 408 in 1920) out of Persia and give it to the Russian Empire, the British colonial empire and the Ottomans although Persia declared neutrality and stayed sovereign: all adjusted to the 1914 frontier with occupation events (counterpart for the British is british-colonial-empire, the Name that Cliopatria uses; if the British Empire rows are merged under british-empire the counterpart string needs to follow). Cliopatria ends the Qajar in 1923 and starts the Pahlavi in 1924, but the pages end the Qajar state on 31 October 1925: a new keyframe qajar-dynasty_1924 (1924-1925) covers the gap and the Pahlavi dossier should start in 1925 or 1926. Qajar to Pahlavi is a dynasty change on the same land (rule 2); the colour agent may want one colour.

Unsettled: whether the Erivan, Karabakh and Ganja khanates in 1796-1806 were provinces or vassals (the pages show support, a settlement and submissions to Russia, not a status; ledger gains at confidence 1). The Shirvan, Sheki and Baku additions of 1797 are undated by any page opened. The Qajar Iran page and the Russian-war page give different dates for Russia's annexation of Kartli-Kakheti (12 September 1801 against December 1800) and for the Turkmenchay signing (10 February against 2 February 1828). The Agha Mohammad Khan page contradicts itself on Shusha (a settlement in 1795; killed 'three days after he had taken the city' in 1797). The Treaty of Akhal (21 September 1881) and the 1884 transfer of Merv, Sarakhs and Ashgabat change no Cliopatria cell. The Seistan arbitration, the Ottoman frontier treaties, the Anglo-Russian Convention of 1907 and Soviet-Persian treaty were not opened (page budget of 9); the first Herat campaigns of Mohammad Shah are undated on the Qajar Iran page. The page is silent on when the British left Persia in 1920-21 (events at confidence 1).

Counterparts that need dossiers: the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic (written by this batch as a rebel state, slug persian-socialist-soviet-republic); the Karabakh, Ganja and Erivan khanates (named as counterparts by string; the eu-19 group's khanates-of-the-caucasus row covers them only to 1796). Gazetteer names the gazetteer lacks: Shusha, Anzali (Bandar-e Anzali, Enzeli), Mughan Plain, Talysh, Erivan Khanate (used only as text or avoided); Khoi is spelled Khoy in places.jsonl.

FIX fx-14 2026-11-01 (F094, conflict with khanate-of-kalat 1794-1822, 400 cells a year in Sistan and Baluchestan, 5 in Baluchistan, 1 in Nimroz). Cliopatria's Qajar outline is modern Iran; the Khanate of Kalat page and the Sistan and Baluchestan province page put Persian Baluchistan with Kalat from Nasir Khan I. Keyframes 1794, 1796, 1797, 1800, 1805, 1806, 1811 and 1822 now subtract it, and a 1828 gain from khanate-of-kalat mirrors Kalat's loss. Not changed: 4 cells of Pakistani Makran (25.3-26.7 N, 61.7-63.2 E) that Cliopatria's Iran outline touches in 1828-1924; the size rule gives them to Kalat, as the 1896 border does. Pages: Khanate of Kalat, Sistan and Baluchestan province.

Fix fx-45 (2 Nov 2026), start. The dossier begins on 2 April 1779 instead of 1789: the Agha Mohammad Khan page has him conquer Mazandaran then, take Gilan in 1782, Qazvin and Zanjan after it, Isfahan on 2 May (1785), Hamadan in summer 1785 and make Tehran his capital on 12 March 1786 and see himself 'as the king of Iran' in 1785-1786, while the infobox and 'Thus 1789 is marked as the start of his reign' give the enthronement; the zand-dynasty ledger already hands this land to qajar-dynasty from 1779, so with a start of 1789 it was nobody's land for up to 1,663 cells in 1782-1788. The 1789 found event became a found of Mazandaran in 1779 and six mirror gains (Semnan 1781, Gilan and Qazvin/Zanjan 1782, Tehran and Hamadan 1785, Isfahan May 1785); the other Zand losses (Kurdish country, Bakhtiari, Alborz-Qom-Markazi, Golestan, northern Yazd, Isfahan 1788) arrive through the Zand ledger alone. The identity start of the Qajar dynasty proper stays 1789 on the pages (infobox 'Establishment: 1789').
